::: {.visual-explainer .explainer-repair}

Can a repair learned on one fine-tune help the next? I fine-tuned Goodfire’s four-layer,
67-million-parameter language model to raise German next-token loss while penalizing changes to
English, French, Spanish and Italian predictions. The objective omitted Dutch, whose loss rose too.
A **repair** is a weight update fit to restore the original Dutch predictions and keep the fine-tuned
predictions in the other five languages. [Goodfire’s model](https://www.goodfire.com/research/interpreting-lm-parameters) · [Selective editing](../selective-editing/explainer.qmd)

Starting from an earlier repair helped most with little fitting text and few steps. At the largest
budget, a repair trained from scratch nearly caught up.

## Three ways to fit a repair {#the-same-starting-repair-two-ways-to-reuse-it}

The two **targets** reuse a repair learned on one earlier fine-tune, the **donor**. All three
fine-tunes used the same base model and recipe, with different seeds and samples of Europarl text.

The repair adds a **rank-one update** $E=ba^\top$ to each of 24 weight matrices. The input vector $a$
reads one scalar $a^\top x$ from $x$. The output vector $b$ writes the correction $Ex=b(a^\top x)$.

- **Scalar-only fitting** learns one multiplier per matrix to rescale or reverse the donor’s correction along the same line.
- **Donor initialization** refits both vectors from their donor values. Their lengths and directions can change.
- **Fresh initialization** also fits both vectors. It starts with a random input vector and a zero output vector in each matrix.

## Refitting the vectors recovers more {#keeping-the-directions-leaves-damage-behind}

**Recovery** is the share of extra Dutch prediction loss the repair removes. At 100%, loss is back at
the base model’s level. I evaluated the selected repairs on **92 Europarl session dates** separate from
fitting and checkpoint selection.

At each budget, the methods use the same fitting text. **Fit tokens** count distinct prediction positions.
A step cap sets the latest checkpoint eligible for selection.

```{=html}
<p id="repair-full-primary" class="explainer-finding">Donor initialization improved recovery over the expanded scalar
search by 11.3 percentage points on the primary target (95% paired interval [10.0, 12.7]) and 20.4 points
on replication ([19.0, 21.7]). Both intervals exceeded the study's 3-point margin.</p>
```

The donor-initialized and scalar-only repairs preserved the German effect and passed the other readout
checks. Other coefficients could recover more under the same repair size limit. [Expanded scalar search](index.qmd#sec-app-checks)

## The donor start helps most in short, low-data runs {#the-donor-helps-most-when-fitting-is-constrained}

With **256 fit tokens and a 50-step cap**, donor initialization led the first fresh start by **4.4** and
**4.1 percentage points** on the primary and replication targets. At **2,048 tokens and a 600-step cap**,
the leads fell to **1.1** and **1.4 points**. The smaller budget included one fresh seed.

Across the regular search, scalar-only recovery stayed within **86.9–87.4%** on the primary target
and **76.3–77.4%** on replication.
